quest.title: The World of Aranara
quest.description: Finally, you meet the mysterious Aranara again. According to Arana, you need to visit Vanarana and find Bija to help Rana. Moreover, you have to play the Rhythm of the Great Dream before getting to the world of Aranara. Head back to Vimara Village, and ask Amadhiah if he has any instrument that you can borrow.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x400, Primogem x50, Mora x40000, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4, Stories of You and the Aranara x1

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But... Do we really have to sing? What if it attracts a Whopperflower?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well... I think using a musical instrument works too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, it's worth a try. Let's return to Vimara Village and see if Grandpa Amadhiah has one!

talks.objective: Return to Vimara Village and talk to Amadhiah

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Grandpa Amadhiah...

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: Oh, Rana's friends... Unfortunately, Rana should be patrolling the forest today.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Let's keep it from him...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, we know! We're here to ask if you have a musical instrument that you can lend us.

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: A musical instrument... Give me a minute, I will go get it.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Amadhiah fetches an old musical instrument from inside.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It looks like... a Mondstadt-style instrument! Grandpa Amadhiah, can you lend it to us?

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: A very, very long time ago... I met a bard in the forest. She gave me this lyre as a keepsake.

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: "Dreams of the garden, memories of the forest... The pomegranate sings, the apples clap..."

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: What a beautiful tune...

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: I'll lend it to you. Use it to light up the darkness in the forest, and perhaps it'll reach her ears...

choices.text: We'll take good care of it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! We'll return it to you, Grandpa Amadhiah! Thanks!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This place is like a village...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, do you remember the small stone houses we saw while camping with Rana?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Those small round houses we saw.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: They're all over this place. It's like a kingdom for little people...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If this is the "Vanarana" that Arana told us about, it should be the home of the Aranara...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But there's no one here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Are they hiding from us?

choices.text: Maybe Arana's tune will do the trick...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right! Just like she said...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Was it the Rhythm of the Great Dream? Paimon thinks so... "Enter our dreams, our world."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... What if singing attracts a Whopperflower? Let's just play the musical instrument instead!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Oh! Paimon can't wait, for both {NICKNAME}'s performance and the world of Aranara.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Huh? Paimon doesn't sense anything! But you've always had a keen eye, {NICKNAME}...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, maybe we should do as Arana said and sing the tune she taught you...

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: #Oh, it belonged to Nara Varuna... Maybe it's destiny that it's going to another Golden Nara like Nara {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: #{M#She}{F#He} called it the Aranyaka because it's the stories of {M#her}{F#his} adventures in the forest with us Aranara. But those stories are lost.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: #Nara {NICKNAME}, I hope it'll be of help to you. I'm really looking forward to Festival Utsava.

dialogues.speaker: Arakara
dialogues.text: Will need happy Viparyas, but Aranakula hasn't returned yet. Um...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, an Aranara...
Eek! Don't capture me, I'll give Nara "tracer"...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's a "tracer"? Anyway, we won't capture you! Don't be afraid!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #This is Paimon, and {M#he}{F#she} is {NICKNAME}. We're good Nara! What's your name?
Oh... You're good Nara, great. Hmm, it was Arana who taught you that tune, right?

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: I'm Arama. Arana may trust both of you, but everyone here is very scared seeing Nara in Vanarana.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: I was afraid. But the Golden Nara has been to many places. The tiny dandelions and spores with you are all saying that you are a very, very good Nara.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, Aranara can communicate with plants, even spores?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Nara {NICKNAME} understands, Paimon is wrong. If you say that loudly in the forest, plants will be sad, and spores will be angry and might even turn into Fungi.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh! Let's not fuss over the details, shall we?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, is this Vanarana? It feels so similar to the place where we found the treasure, but it is slightly different. It does have a huge rock house, but...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Feeling a little disappointed?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It isn't what Paimon expected! Paimon thought Vanarana would be a lively Aranara village where everyone would be dancing Aranara dances, eating Aranara food, completing Aranara commissions...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Paimon's thoughts didn't run that wild!

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Everyone's in Vanarana, but because everyone's afraid, we still can't let both of you inside, even if Nara {NICKNAME} is golden.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What about silver? Is silver bad?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Silver, just like the moon. Very good, very good.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hee-hee... So here isn't Vanarana?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: This isn't Vanarana. Ah, actually... This is Vanarana, but not the real Vanarana.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So is it Vanarana or not...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: If you help Aranara, everyone won't be afraid, and you can enter the real Vanarana. Come with me, help Aranara and get the "tracer."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon gets it now! You mean "treasure"! Sure, we'll help you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What about silver? Is silver rare?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Silver, just like the moon. Very good, very good.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hee-hee... So here isn't Vanarana?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: How strange. Spores are not plants. If you say that loudly in the forest, plants will be sad, and spores will be angry and might even turn into Fungi.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... It feels so similar to the place where we found the treasure, but it is slightly different. It does have a huge rock house, but...

talks.objective: Play the Rhythm of the Great Dream at the designated location

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Look, Vanagni! Be careful... Even if you talk to them, their only response is rage and shooting flames.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...What? It's just a Whopperflower!

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: It's very dangerous! Very dangerous! Let's leave before the Vanagni notices us!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...You aren't really afraid of a Whopperflower, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Anyway, don't worry, Arama. We'll help! Right, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Oh, be careful, Nara {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, we have to get into Vanarana as soon as possible to help Rana.

talks.objective: Complete the trial of the Phantasmal Seed

dialogues.speaker: Arakanta
dialogues.text: There is no doubt that Arakanta is the fastest Aranara. Arakanta, as fast as the Rishboland Tiger.

dialogues.speaker: Arakanta
dialogues.text: If I could run on the back of the Rishboland Tiger...

talks.objective: Play the Rhythm of the Great Dream in front of the strange stone

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, we've helped! So where's the treasure, Arama?

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Isn't "treasure" the incantation to make Nara help?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why isn't Paimon surprised at all?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Did you really think Arama prepared treasure for us?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, how did you learn to use the word "treasure" like that, Arama?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: I've observed Nara, and I noticed that they become very good and very willing to help other Nara once they hear the word "treasure."

choices.text: Some Nara become bad for treasures.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Hmm, I see. I've learned a lot. Thank you, Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: You're amazing! You're good Nara who help Aranara. Now, no one will be afraid to let you enter Vanarana.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: You can enter Vanarana by playing Arana's tune in front of "Silapna."

choices.text: Nara who help for treasures may not be good either.
Nara like Paimon would fall for it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Treasures are great! Don't look down on treasures!

dialogues.speaker: Aranaga
dialogues.text: The Yajna Grass... Must get it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh? This is Vanarana... So many Aranara...

choices.text: It seems like the same place, but...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, Paimon gets it! It feels completely different!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Since we've arrived in Vanarana, it's time to get a Bija and help Rana.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Bija? I've heard the stories about it.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Anyway, this is the real Vanarana, or to be more precise, it's "Mahavanaranapna"...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wh—What a long name! And there are so many "a's"!

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Yes, but we usually don't use its full name because it's too long. If explained in Nara language...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Ah, I know. It's "the Aranara Forest of Dreams".

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Dreams"... So you're saying...

choices.text: That the Vanarana we just saw exists in reality?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Hmm, it's a story from very, very long ago. I wasn't even a seed then, I was still in a slumber in Sarva. But after Vanarana was destroyed once, we started living in this dream.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, interesting past...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: It's very scary! I heard even the sky turned black. Trees swayed like grass on a field under strong winds, and they fell to the ground. And then very, very scary monsters were everywhere.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Luckily, they are all stories, not memories. Anyway, if you wish to leave Vanarana's dream, sing the Rhythm of the Great Dream in front of Silapna, and it's the same to return here.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Come with me. Araja will find a way to get you a Bija.

choices.text: And we're in a dream now?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, according to Arana, we must get a Bija from Vanarana to help Rana.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh? This is Vanarana... So many Aranara...

choices.text: It seems like the same place, but...

response.text: ...But we usually don't use its full name because it's too long. If explained in Nara's language... Ah, I know. It's "Vanarana of Great Dreams".

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #"Dreams"... Speaking of which, we met an Aranara where the researcher was, and {NICKNAME} seems to have had a dream...

choices.text: So the Vanarana we just saw exists in reality?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Come with me. Araja will find a way to get you a Bija.

choices.text: And we're in a dream now?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, according to Arana, we must get a Bija from Vanarana to help Rana.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: #Whoa, a Nara... I haven't seen one in so long. So tall and golden, just like {M#she}{F#he} said. Welcome to Vanarana.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #Yes, Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon. They're amazing! They're not even scared of Vanagni.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: Whoa! Amazing! Nara who used Arana's tune to get into Vanarana are definitely good Nara whom Arana trusts.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's strange. How do all of you know that it was Arana who guided us here?

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: Every Aranara has their own tune, and every tune is different. That's how we know who's home.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: Arana has been making friends with Nara in Avidya Forest and Ardravi Valley, so I haven't seen her for a long time. We heard her tune and thought that it was her. We were very happy.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: #But it was a Nara who entered Vanarana, and it scared us all. So I asked for Arama's help to tell everyone that Nara {NICKNAME} is a good Nara.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon gets it now! But according to Arama, the problems we solved were outside the dream. Was that even helpful? Helpful to Ma... Mahavana...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh! Aranara names are so difficult!

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: The Vanarana in dreams is a shadow of the Vanarana outside. So, things will get better here now that you have dealt with the problems outside. Thank you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Oooh... *cough* Let's get down to business! {NICKNAME}, about Rana...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We need a Bija to help a very important friend of Arana... She's a very important friend of ours too...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell both people... well, both Aranara, the reason for your request...

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: Bija... The last time I prepared a Bija was a long time ago. I heard the Golden Nara and Aramuhukunda were still here then.

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: I had so many stories and so many dreams then. It was so long ago...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Looks like Araja is about to start telling a story!)

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: Those stories aren't my memories anymore, and I shouldn't be the one to tell them. Let's put our focus back on the Bija.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Rana has been seriously harmed by Marana. She needs a Bija as soon as possible...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Arana is a very, very old Aranara whose Ararakalari is very, very powerful! So, Narana's condition won't worsen. As for the Bija...

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: You're right, Narana's condition will be stable with Arana there. However, don't forget that Nara are not trees. They have less time, and it's easier for them to get hurt.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Right! Since Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon are friends with Arana, and they all have the same wish, we should help them.

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: #We'll do our best, but we also need Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon's help to form a Bija...

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: We are going to hold Festival Utsava, but many Aranara are still lingering in the forest. Now that you have the scent of Vanarana, you'll be able to approach them. Tell them it's time to return.

choices.text: Can we really relax like this...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Araja, you mentioned that Nara don't have much time, so shouldn't we get a Bija as soon as possible?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Nara {NICKNAME}, Paimon. According to the stories of the Bija, in order to form a Bija that's healthy, strong, and filled with energy, a Festival Utsava is absolutely necessary.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Regardless of the sorrow we carry, energy for the Bija can only be accumulated if the Nara friends of Aranara and the Aranara friends of Nara celebrate Festival Utsava together.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright... It's not very convincing, but just like how unbelievable Ararakalari is, maybe it's an Ara-ceremony or Ara-festival.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Ah! If we're going to celebrate Festival Utsava, we must get everyone back. A little while ago, Arapandu and some others went to <color=#00E1FFFF>Apam Woods</color>. Besides that, Aranakin and some others should be around <color=#00E1FFFF>Gandha Hill</color>...

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: #Everyone, I'm sure you're not afraid of Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon anymore, so why don't you try becoming friends? I had a Nara friend once, and those memories are still very dear to me.

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: Besides that, you must <color=#00E1FFFF>get a few Vasoma Fruits</color> from the Vasara Trees in Ashvattha's Concourses. Three of them should be enough.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ashvattha... Vasara Tree... Vasoma...

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: #But I haven't been able to leave the dream for a long time, and I don't remember where Ashvattha's Concourses are. I'll leave the finding to Arama and Nara {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #An adventure with Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: An adventure with Arama!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Speaking of which, the incident in Vimara Village is also very concerning. Can we ask other Aranara to find out who's trying to harm the children there?

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: Oh, my! It sounds like something only "Marana's Avatar" is capable of. They aren't stopping with Aranara and are even harming little Nara...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: If it's around Vimara Village, I did see Ararycan near <color=#00E1FFFF>Devantaka Mountain</color> a few suns and moons ago. He was investigating something bad.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #It may be linked to the bad Nara that Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon are looking for!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, that's right. Aranara are very elusive, so they may have seen something suspicious! Besides that, we have many other questions...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: The Vasoma Fruit is a fruit filled with dreams and energy! It isn't as powerful as the Bija, but it's amazing too.

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: A Bija can be formed by feeding a Vasoma Fruit to the Ashvattha Tree. It's a great tree planted by Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, and it's the origin of Aranara.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, it really caught Paimon's attention just now because Iotham mentioned something similar too...

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: It's a story from very long ago...

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: A long time ago, Aranara walked the earth and made friends with Nara and all living creatures. There was no Marana then. Until a disaster that occurred many, many moons ago...

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata returned to Sarva, and Marana's rampage through the earth began. Once the forest recovered its vitality, the Aranara hid the real Vanarana in a dream to protect themselves.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... So that's when Marana came into existence?

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: The forest didn't know death, until a day came when the trees realized that withered flowers and dead animals covered the earth.

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: On the same day, the earth remembered the dark, poisonous blood it had once devoured, or was about to devour. The rivers thought of the descent of the sun, evaporating all water and leaving a red world behind.

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: They realized that all things would meet their end, and so, Marana was born. It is the name of death, and those who know it shall die.

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: Marana urges everything towards death. As for the tall, dark, and warped beings, they are the avatars chosen by Marana, the heralds of death.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's why Iotham was afraid of the Fatui... They are tall, and they wear black...

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: Of course. In my stories, Marana's Avatar takes many forms. Sometimes beasts, sometimes birds, sometimes Nara, sometimes blight...

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: But stories are just stories, and they aren't my memories.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hmm... Let Paimon think for a moment. {NICKNAME}. There's so much for us to do.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We must find Ashvattha to... get a va-something? Then go to <color=#00E1FFFF>Devantaka Mountain</color> to look for Ara... Ararycan? Is that right? Then we have to find Arapandu in <color=#00E1FFFF>Apam Woods</color> and Aranakin in <color=#00E1FFFF>Gandha Hill</color>...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Argh! Ugh! Aranara names are so difficult!

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon, this is for you.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: I've been observing. Nara must use this to remember. Otherwise, Nara memories will get messed up and won't be able to form a story.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is that... an old notebook?

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: #Oh, it belonged to Nara Varuna... Maybe it's destiny that it's going to another Golden Nara like Nara {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: #{M#She}{F#He} called it the Aranyaka because it's the stories of {M#her}{F#his} adventures in the forest with us Aranara. But those stories are lost.

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: #Nara {NICKNAME}, I hope it'll be of help to you. I'm really looking forward to Festival Utsava.

choices.text: As long as it helps Rana.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, you're right. We'll ask Araja later if we have more questions!

response.speaker: Paimon

response.text: Araja, you mentioned that Nara don't have much time, so shouldn't we get a Bija as soon as possible?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, no! That's completely wrong! We don't have time for festivals! Araja mentioned that Nara don't have much time, so shouldn't we get a Bija as soon as possible?

choices.text: What do you need us to do?

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: Yes, we need Nara's help to form a Bija.

choices.text: It's urgent. We don't have time to waste.

talks.objective: Go to the place that Arama mentioned
Play the Rhythm of the Great Dream in front of Silapna

dialogues.speaker: Arapacati
dialogues.text: Is my brothers' cooking training going smoothly?

talks.objective: Head to the house and talk to Araja

dialogues.speaker: Araesha
dialogues.text: The unseen and uncatchable that slips past the moon's gaze and encourages the growth of sprouts... This is so simple that any Aranara can immediately get the answer... I need another riddle.

dialogues.speaker: Arakavi
dialogues.text: Ah, Arama, you bring a Nara with you... Looks like my guess is correct.

dialogues.speaker: Araprabhu
dialogues.text: Training on Ararakalari... Mustn't slack off!

dialogues.speaker: Araprabhu
dialogues.text: A Nara. A lost Nara?

dialogues.speaker: Aramani
dialogues.text: What's the expression in Nara language... "Honest price," no? I don't understand, totally don't understand.

dialogues.speaker: Aralila
dialogues.text: Aranishat, you should admit defeat. Don't be like a stubborn twig that refuses to bend against strong gusts. You will break just like it.

dialogues.speaker: Aranishat
dialogues.text: Aralila, let's have another match after the moon sinks and the sun rises again!

dialogues.speaker: Aravinay
dialogues.text: Staffs are like trees, each with distinct disposition...

dialogues.speaker: Arayash
dialogues.text: Golden Nara...

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: #Whoa, a Nara... I haven't seen one in so long. So tall and golden, just like {M#she}{F#he} said. Welcome to Vanarana.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #Yes, Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon. They're amazing! They're not even scared of Vanagni.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: Whoa! Amazing! Nara who used Arana's tune to get into Vanarana are definitely good Nara whom Arana trusts.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's strange. How do all of you know that it was Arana who guided us here?

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: Every Aranara has their own tune, and every tune is different. That's how we know who's home.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: Arana has been making friends with Nara in Avidya Forest and Ardravi Valley, so I haven't seen her for a long time. We heard her tune and thought that it was her. We were very happy.

dialogues.speaker: Araja
dialogues.text: #But it was a Nara who entered Vanarana, and it scared us all. So I asked for Arama's help to tell everyone that Nara {NICKNAME} is a good Nara.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon gets it now! But according to Arama, the problems we solved were outside the dream. Was that even helpful? Helpful to Ma... Mahavana...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh! Aranara names are so difficult!

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: The Vanarana in dreams is a shadow of the Vanarana outside. So, things will get better here now that you have dealt with the problems outside. Thank you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Oooh... *cough* Let's get down to business! {NICKNAME}, about Rana...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We need a Bija to help a very important friend of Arana... She's a very important friend of ours too...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell both people... well, both Aranara, the reason for your request...

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: Bija... The last time I prepared a Bija was a long time ago. I heard the Golden Nara and Aramuhukunda were still here then.

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: I had so many stories and so many dreams then. It was so long ago...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Looks like Araja is about to start telling a story!)

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: Those stories aren't my memories anymore, and I shouldn't be the one to tell them. Let's put our focus back on the Bija.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Rana has been seriously harmed by Marana. She needs a Bija as soon as possible...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Arana is a very, very old Aranara whose Ararakalari is very, very powerful! So, Narana's condition won't worsen. As for the Bija...

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: You're right, Narana's condition will be stable with Arana there. However, don't forget that Nara are not trees. They have less time, and it's easier for them to get hurt.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Right! Since Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon are friends with Arana, and they all have the same wish, we should help them.

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: #We'll do our best, but we also need Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon's help to form a Bija...

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: We are going to hold Festival Utsava, but many Aranara are still lingering in the forest. Now that you have the scent of Vanarana, you'll be able to approach them. Tell them it's time to return.

choices.text: Can we really relax like this...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Araja, you mentioned that Nara don't have much time, so shouldn't we get a Bija as soon as possible?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Nara {NICKNAME}, Paimon. According to the stories of the Bija, in order to form a Bija that's healthy, strong, and filled with energy, a Festival Utsava is absolutely necessary.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Regardless of the sorrow we carry, energy for the Bija can only be accumulated if the Nara friends of Aranara and the Aranara friends of Nara celebrate Festival Utsava together.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright... It's not very convincing, but just like how unbelievable Ararakalari is, maybe it's an Ara-ceremony or Ara-festival.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Ah! If we're going to celebrate Festival Utsava, we must get everyone back. A little while ago, Arapandu and some others went to <color=#00E1FFFF>Apam Woods</color>. Besides that, Aranakin and some others should be around <color=#00E1FFFF>Gandha Hill</color>...

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: #Everyone, I'm sure you're not afraid of Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon anymore, so why don't you try becoming friends? I had a Nara friend once, and those memories are still very dear to me.

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: Besides that, you must <color=#00E1FFFF>get a few Vasoma Fruits</color> from the Vasara Trees in Ashvattha's Concourses. Three of them should be enough.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ashvattha... Vasara Tree... Vasoma...

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: #But I haven't been able to leave the dream for a long time, and I don't remember where Ashvattha's Concourses are. I'll leave the finding to Arama and Nara {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #An adventure with Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: An adventure with Arama!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Speaking of which, the incident in Vimara Village is also very concerning. Can we ask other Aranara to find out who's trying to harm the children there?

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: Oh, my! It sounds like something only "Marana's Avatar" is capable of. They aren't stopping with Aranara and are even harming little Nara...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: If it's around Vimara Village, I did see Ararycan near <color=#00E1FFFF>Devantaka Mountain</color> a few suns and moons ago. He was investigating something bad.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #It may be linked to the bad Nara that Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon are looking for!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, that's right. Aranara are very elusive, so they may have seen something suspicious! Besides that, we have many other questions...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: The Vasoma Fruit is a fruit filled with dreams and energy! It isn't as powerful as the Bija, but it's amazing too.

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: A Bija can be formed by feeding a Vasoma Fruit to the Ashvattha Tree. It's a great tree planted by the Lord of Verdure, and it's the origin of Aranara.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, it really caught Paimon's attention just now because Iotham mentioned something similar too...

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: It's a story from very long ago...

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: A long time ago, Aranara walked the earth and made friends with Nara and all living creatures. There was no Marana then. Until a disaster that occurred many, many moons ago...

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: Many returned to Sarva, and the Marana's rampage through the earth began. Once the forest recovered its vitality, the Aranara hid the real Vanarana in a dream to protect themselves.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... So that's when Marana came into existence?

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: The forest didn't know death, until a day came when the trees realized that withered flowers and dead animals covered the earth.

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: On the same day, the earth remembered the dark, poisonous blood it had once devoured, or was about to devour. The rivers thought of the descent of the sun, evaporating all water and leaving a red world behind.

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: They realized that all things would meet their end, and so, Marana was born. It is the name of death, and those who know it shall die.

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: Marana urges everything towards death. As for the tall, dark, and warped beings, they are the avatars chosen by Marana, the heralds of death.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's why Iotham was afraid of the Fatui... They are tall, and they wear black...

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: Of course. In my stories, Marana's Avatar takes many forms. Sometimes beasts, sometimes birds, sometimes Nara, sometimes blight...

response.speaker: Araja
response.text: But stories are just stories, and they aren't my memories.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hmm... Let Paimon think for a moment. {NICKNAME}. There's so much for us to do.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We must find Ashvattha to... get a va-something? Then go to <color=#00E1FFFF>Devantaka Mountain</color> to look for Ara... Ararycan? Is that right? Then we have to find Arapandu in <color=#00E1FFFF>Apam Woods</color> and Aranakin in <color=#00E1FFFF>Gandha Hill</color>...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Argh! Ugh! Aranara names are so difficult!

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon, this is for you.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: I've been observing. Nara must use this to remember. Otherwise, Nara memories will get messed up and won't be able to form a story.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is that... an old notebook?

choices.text: As long as it helps Rana.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, you're right. We'll ask Araja later if we have more questions!
